topics.topic: MSU plan TSR hurdle of 20% for 100% payout; whether hurdles are shareholder-friendly
topics.stated_position: Management believes the 100% payout target for delivering 20% TSR is appropriate; TSR is absolute rather than relative, so the annual MSU award is split into two grants each year to smooth short-term market volatility; the compensation committee reviews and approves all compensation practices, and in 2020 the TSR hurdle was raised from 10% to 20% due in part to shareholder feedback.
topics.quote: In 2020, we increased our TSR hurdle from 10% to 20%, due in part to shareholder feedback. We appreciate your feedback and will provide it to our compensation committee. The committee determines threshold payments annually.

topics.topic: Exclusion of incentive compensation costs from Adjusted EBITDA in the annual incentive plan
topics.stated_position: Adjusted EBITDA is based on a "pre-bonus" number to incorporate the underlying performance of the business; the company monitors the "sharing ratio" (projected bonus payout as a percentage of Adjusted EBITDA) and the Board has discretion to limit the bonus if the sharing ratio is not aligned with expectations.
topics.quote: We carefully monitor the impact of incremental Adjusted Revenue on the bonus by measuring the “sharing ratio,” expressed as projected bonus payout as a percentage of Adjusted EBITDA. Our Board of Directors has the discretion to limit the bonus if the sharing ratio is not aligned with expectations.

topics.topic: Decline in compensation and benefit expense per employee
topics.stated_position: Management confirmed adjusted operating expense per average employee declined, due in part to the increased proportion of the employee base located in India where labor costs are lower, and to efforts to control costs in discretionary categories including professional fees, travel, and marketing.
topics.quote: Those expenses have declined on a per employee basis, due in part to the increased proportion of our employee base located in India, where our labor costs are lower than in many other markets. The decline also reflects our efforts to control costs in other discretionary categories including professional fees, travel, and marketing.

topics.topic: Differentiation and go-to-market for Morningstar Sustainalytics' climate suite
topics.stated_position: Climate solutions are differentiated by detailed asset-level data and ratings that provide insights into management structure and actions; three areas of focus for the remainder of the year are increasing ESG thought leadership and voice, better leveraging the broader Morningstar sales teams, and leveraging index capabilities as a delivery channel for all climate intellectual property.
topics.quote: Finally, with the closer alignment of Morningstar Sustainalytics and Morningstar Indexes, we are leveraging our index capabilities as a delivery channel for all our climate intellectual property. This enables us to offer clients end-to-end solutions from portfolio construction to implementation, while leveraging the go-to-market footprint of Morningstar Indexes.

topics.topic: Disclosure of flows for asset-based products
topics.stated_position: The company is evaluating more frequent disclosures of net flows to its asset-based products, and noted Managed Portfolios is Investment Management's flagship offering and the focus of recent investments.
topics.quote: We’re evaluating more frequent disclosures of net flows to our asset-based products. In the meantime, we can share that Morningstar Indexes and Workplace Solutions both experienced positive net inflows for the year-to-date through June 2023.

topics.topic: PitchBook versus FactSet and MSCI in private markets
topics.stated_position: PitchBook offers more extensive private market coverage across all entity types than FactSet or MSCI, and its suite of tools supports core private market workflows; "FactSet and MSCI lack comparable workflow functionalities."
topics.quote: PitchBook offers more extensive private market coverage across all entity types (companies, investors, deals, funds, and service providers) than FactSet or MSCI.

topics.topic: Whether PitchBook will expand into KYC/AML, risk, compliance and trade credit use cases
topics.stated_position: Management is focused on executing its plan in PitchBook's core business and does not see know-your-customer or anti-money-laundering use cases as a core part of PitchBook's current strategy at this time, though they could be potential areas of future expansion, possibly in partnership with third-party application developers.
topics.quote: We are focused on executing our plan in PitchBook’s core business, where we see significant opportunities. While entirely legitimate use cases, we do not see know-your-customer or anti-money-laundering use cases as a core part of PitchBook’s current strategy at this time.

topics.topic: Integration of Leveraged Commentary & Data (LCD) into PitchBook
topics.stated_position: Management stated it is in the process of integrating LCD research, news, and data into the PitchBook platform, and that LCD-related revenue is not currently included in reported PitchBook revenue.
topics.quote: Leveraged Commentary & Data (LCD), which includes private credit and leveraged loan data and research. Note that we are in the process of integrating LCD research, news, and data into the PitchBook platform. LCD-related revenue is not currently included in the revenue we report for PitchBook.

topics.stated_position: Mansueto has filed annual 10b5-1 plans to sell a portion of his shares to diversify his investments, has never suspended a plan once filed, uses dollar-cost averaging and simple trading rules designed to minimize downward pressure on the share price; the 2023 pause reflected the SEC's longer cooling-off period.
topics.quote: Joe has never suspended a 10b5-1 plan once it has been filed. He has set simple trading rules designed to minimize downward pressure on the Morningstar share price and allow for the plan to complete its sales over the course of a year. He uses a dollar-cost-averaging approach to his sales.

notable_language.quote: Our goal is to have pay structures that are aligned with best practices and the committee works closely with external consultants and considers industry benchmarks and peer practices to determine what’s best for Morningstar.
notable_language.why_notable: Defensive framing in response to a pointed shareholder challenge that the plan is not shareholder-friendly; appeals to benchmarks rather than addressing the hurdle's difficulty.

notable_language.quote: Your example highlights the myriad of ways that PitchBook data can be used and underscores its value.
notable_language.why_notable: Turns a question about a strategic gap into a promotional claim about the data asset — a rhetorical redirect rather than an answer.

notable_language.quote: Yes, you’re correct that that adjusted operating expense per average employee declined in the first quarter of 2023, relative to the prior-year period, a trend that continued into the second quarter of 2023 relative to the prior-year period.
notable_language.why_notable: Unusually direct confirmation of an investor's inference about declining per-employee compensation, tied openly to offshoring to India.

notable_language.quote: Managed Portfolios, Investment Management’s flagship offering which accounts for a large share of its revenue and is the focus of our recent investments, experienced positive net inflows for the year-to-date through June 2023, driven by strong net flows outside the U.S. while flows in the U.S. were close to flat.
notable_language.why_notable: Characterises Managed Portfolios as the flagship and investment focus, while conceding U.S. flows were flat — a hedge inside a positive statement.
